ai.title: Cloud history project types gain remove semantics
ai.summary: The shared Cloud history contract in `common/src/desktop-cloud/history.ts` now models project removal. `CloudHistoryProject` gains an optional `removedAt` timestamp indicating when a user removed a project, which is absent from older servers. `CloudHistoryProjectUpdate` changes from a single shape to a union that allows setting a name, toggling removal with a boolean flag, or both, while chats and files are retained. This type change supports a PATCH mechanism where removing a project keeps its data but excludes it from lists until a new prompt is made.
ai.evidence: The diff adds a removedAt?: string | null field to `CloudHistoryProject` and changes `CloudHistoryProjectUpdate` from a single-object type to a union type including removed?: boolean in `common/src/desktop-cloud/history.ts`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which client or server code consumes the new `removedAt` field or implements the corresponding PATCH handler.

eli5.text: Freebuff's cloud service now supports removing a project from your visible list while keeping its chats and files stored on the server. This is an internal system update that defines how the assistant handles project removal, and it is in place but does nothing yet because the actual client and server code that uses it is not part of this change. You will not notice any difference in your daily use of the assistant until the feature is fully connected and released.

The client also exposes a new `deleteSite` method that validates a site identifier and issues a DELETE request to the `/${siteId}` endpoint, enabling programmatic site teardown.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/sites/client.ts`, the diff adds a `site_deleting` entry to the `knownErrors` map and introduces a `deleteSite` method that issues a DELETE request to the site endpoint.

eli5.text: The Freebuff Sites feature now shows a specific message when a site is in the middle of being deleted, rather than a generic conflict error. It also adds the ability to programmatically remove a site by sending a deletion request. This update applies to developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK who manage hosted sites. You will notice that deletion attempts now provide a clearer status, and the system supports tearing down sites directly.

ai.title: Stream interruption messages distinguish missing metadata from network
ai.summary: Stream interruption error messages in the SDK and agent runtime no longer attribute missing completion metadata to a network drop; they now state that a supported completion signal was missing, which may indicate either a connection issue or an incompatible provider stream. The `REPEATED_STREAM_INTERRUPTIONS_MESSAGE` constant in `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/stream-parser.ts` was updated to reflect this broader cause. Additionally, `classifyThrownStreamRecovery` in `sdk/src/impl/stream-interruption.ts` now returns fixed message and detail strings instead of propagating the shared recovery object, preventing transport exceptions that echo credentials or URLs from leaking into the user-facing conversation notes. These changes refine the classification of stream endings across the agent loop's auto-retry path.
ai.evidence: The diff in `sdk/src/impl/stream-interruption.ts` updates the `STREAM_INTERRUPTED_RECOVERY` message from claiming a connection drop to stating that a supported completion signal was missing, and `classifyThrownStreamRecovery` now returns fixed strings for `message` and `detail` instead of relying on the shared recovery object to prevent leaking transport error details.

changes.what: Updated stream interruption and thrown error recovery messages to avoid falsely attributing missing metadata to network failures and to prevent leaking raw transport details.
Revised the repeated stream interruptions error message and comment to describe missing completion metadata or incompatible provider responses instead of dropped connections.
Updated internal comment in the stream prompt handler to align with the broader definition of stream interruptions that includes incompatible provider streams.

eli5.text: The error messages shown when the assistant struggles to receive a complete answer from a model now describe the issue more accurately. Instead of assuming your internet connection dropped, the assistant explains that it received a response missing expected finishing details, which could be due to a connection issue or a model that does not send standard completion signals. The details provided to the user also no longer include sensitive technical information that might contain account keys or links. This is an internal fix that improves the clarity of error messages when an AI response fails; no action is required.

ai.summary: Sponsored surveys expand to support `ranking` and `text` question kinds, alongside new advertiser targeting via country selection and time-based scheduling in the `common` package. ai.title: Gemini thought signature replay and backfill in OpenAI-compatible tool
ai.summary: The OpenAI-compatible provider in packages/llm-providers/ now captures the extra_content (Gemini's thought signature) on tool calls and replays it on the next request, tagging it with the producing model so signatures are not mixed across models. The agent runtime stores the provider metadata on the history's tool-call part rather than the call itself, and the SDK's BYOK transform backfills Google's documented placeholder (skip_thought_signature_validator) for unsigned calls, preventing the HTTP 400 that Gemini 3 returns when a replayed call lacks a signature.
ai.evidence: New constants GEMINI_API_HOST and GEMINI_SKIP_THOUGHT_SIGNATURE in sdk/src/impl/byok-request.ts, and the backfillGeminiThoughtSignatures function which adds extra_content.google.thought_signature = 'skip_thought_signature_validator' to unsigned assistant tool calls.

changes.what: Added extra_content support to the OpenAI-compatible chat provider to capture and replay Gemini thought signatures on tool calls.
Stored provider metadata on the history's tool-call part and extended the stream parser to pass provider options through to tool execution callbacks.
Added backfill logic for Gemini thought signatures in BYOK requests and propagated tool-call provider metadata in the SDK stream.
